title: PHP request memory corruption flaws permit unauthenticated remote code execution
summary: PHP reports two request-handling memory corruption flaws allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. The highest documented risk is mod_php, where a request can trigger exploitation before application code runs.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated requests reach memory corruption and code execution in web-serving PHP. Both vulnerabilities are in CISA KEV, requiring a 24-hour response under the feed rubric.

affected.note: PHP 8.1 and older require a vendor backport or migration to a supported fixed branch.

exposure: Relevant to PHP serving web requests, including FPM, mod_php, CGI, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Do not assume application authentication protects request initialization.

params.instructions: Check the web-serving PHP runtime against 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12 for its branch; confirm vendor backports separately. CLI version alone may differ from workers.

remediation.details: Update to the patched release for the PHP branch or obtain a vendor-confirmed backport, then restart workers. Partial configuration mitigations are not complete fixes.
remediation.risk: Medium. Worker restarts interrupt requests; branch migrations require application compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm running web workers use a fixed package after restart.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Added the PHP Project's published Critical rating for both vulnerabilities after independent review identified the omission.

exploitation.note: Both CVEs were added to CISA KEV on October 26, 2026.
